metadata.levers: Calculate across documents; State the rounding

sections.evidence:
- D06 (Q19, para 87, L282) [c1]: "each Big Four firm could be restricted to auditing 65 of the FTSE 350 companies"
- D02 (appendix 20.4, L616) [c1]: "Firms outside the four largest currently perform 11 audits of the FTSE 350 today"
- D02 (appendix 20.4, L616) [c1]: "in order to hold a 20% share of the FTSE 350 audit market in the next five years, firms other than the four largest would need to win about 60 tenders"
sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: a per-firm limit from one response turned into audits that must change hands, timed at the yearly rate another response's estimate implies; medium; measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: D06 L282 (65 per Big Four firm) -> 4 × 65 = 260 -> 350 − 260 = 90 outside the Big Four; D02 L616 (11 audits held, about 60 wins in five years) -> 90 − 11 = 79 wins; 60 / 5 = 12 a year; 79 / 12 = 6.58 -> 7 years. Minimal inputs: 65, 11, 60 wins, five years; 350 from the index's name.
- Universe: not applicable (one derived number).
- Necessity: D06 supplies the individual cap of 65; the only other per-firm limits in the bundle are BDO's own 60 and "say 50" (D01 L145, L221), a different respondent's proposal, and ICAEW's collective "around 60%" (D06 L408), which the question excludes by "individual". D02 supplies the rate (about 60 tender wins in five years) and the 11 audits held; a search of all ten documents for tender counts finds only D04 note 4 (8 of 29 tendering companies changed auditor), which gives no forward rate. Without D06 the cap is unknown; without D02 there is no rate. No single passage holds both. No removal probes run (optional diagnostics, none requested).
- Selected-lever checks: not a which-items question, no decoy required. State the rounding: 6.58 rounds to 7; one decimal place would split the stated bases (6.6 and 6.7), so whole years is the supported precision.
- Targeted failure modes: (1) Part vs total: 90 / 12 = 7.5, given as 8 years (or 7.5), when the 11 audits already held (D02 L616) are not taken off; set by the same paragraph that gives the rate. (2) Look-alike measure: ICAEW's collective cap "of around 60%" (D06 L408, Appendix A): 60% of 350 = 210, 350 − 210 = 140, 140 − 11 = 129, 129 / 12 = 10.75, 11 years. Considered and not declared: scaling the five years by 90 / 70 = 6.43, 6 years (no trap definition names a proportional short cut); reading 65 companies as 65% (9.3, 9 years; the paragraph says "65 of the FTSE 350 companies"); adding D02 L91's "one to two years before these audits go live" (the question asks for years of wins). No measured attempts yet: align the modes with the run's observed wrong answers before Submit.
- Calculation verification: script, 2026-10-12: 4 × 65 = 260; 350 − 260 = 90; 90 − 11 = 79; 60 / 5 = 12; 79 / 12 = 6.583; 12 × 6 = 72; 79 − 72 = 7 > 6. Units: audits (companies), tender wins, years. Rounding to the nearest whole year, half-up or half-even alike.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: bundle overview lists "65 clients market cap", "60% collective Big Four market share cap", "20% target for FTSE350 audits by outside firms" and "60% of all tenders required to reach target"; none gives 11, 60 tenders, 79 or 7. Searches: "65" (D06 L53, L282 only), "tender" with figures (D02, D04 note 4), "audits of the FTSE 350" (D02 L616). Shortest complete route found is the eight steps above.
- Precision/readings: present audits outside the Big Four are stated as 11 (D02 L616), 3% (D02 L254, 10.5), 98% inside (D02 L67, 7) and by "sevenfold" (D02 L89, 10); with each base's own five-year wins (59 to 63) the result is 6.58, 6.68, 6.59, 6.67 years, and 6.69 with exactly 59 wins: 7 on every one. Mixed inputs (83 wins at 12 a year) give 6.92: still 7. "would bring" is the least time, every Big Four firm at its cap; the bundle gives no per-firm holdings. ICAEW's "around 65 clients for any single firm" (D06 L53) and "65 of the FTSE 350 companies" (L282) agree.
- Completeness: no known source gaps (10 of 10 documents read in full; hashes match the capture).
- Style/set review: plain wording, respondents named as organisations, no file or page references; 30 words. First question on this bundle; i02 uses the same Deloitte paragraph and is an alternate, not a second question.
- Warnings answered: see the floor output recorded in notes/session.md; the form will flag 11 for Doc 2 in Steps 2 and 5 (printed at character 83,552, beyond the range the form reads): expected false alarm, quoted in Evidence.

sections.question: At the yearly rate of tender wins Deloitte's five-year target assumes, how many years of wins, to the nearest whole year, would bring the Big Four within ICAEW's individual cap?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 6, reply on how a cap should be measured): besides a collective cap, ICAEW describes an individual one, under which each Big Four firm could be restricted to auditing 65 of the FTSE 350 companies.
Step 2. Source input (Doc 2, appendix reply on whether a cap's benefits could be realised): firms outside the four largest currently perform 11 audits of the FTSE 350. To hold a 20% share in the next five years they would need to win about 60 tenders.
Step 3. Calculation (Doc 6): with every Big Four firm at the individual cap, the four together audit 4 × 65 = 260 companies.
Step 4. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): the rest of the index would be left to other firms: 350 − 260 = 90 companies.
Step 5. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): those firms already hold some of them, so the wins still needed are 90 − 11 = 79.
Step 6. Calculation (Doc 2): the target's wins spread over its five years give a yearly rate of 60 / 5 = 12 wins.
Step 7. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): six years at that rate bring 12 × 6 = 72 wins.
Step 8. Final answer (Doc 2 and Doc 6): 79 − 72 = 7 wins are still missing after six years, more than half of one year's 12, so the time needed is closer to seven years than to six. To the nearest whole year: 7 years.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Part vs total
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Look-alike measure
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

Why these are traps: Part vs total: Doc 2 says other firms already perform 11 FTSE 350 audits; counting all 90 audits outside the cap as wins gives 8 years. Look-alike measure: Doc 6's summary also gives a collective cap of around 60%; using it gives 11 years. The gold counts 79 wins.
